M08 viewport streaming follow-up: two Codex P2 findings on PR #992 (branch `codex/run-41474031461-1`, already merged with main through hover cards #991 and with reserved points promoted to the always-visible batch — keep those). Continue on that branch. apps/web only.

FINDING 1 — truncated cells never refine at close zoom (`apps/web/src/lib/spatial/galaxy-star-cells.ts` ~line 132): a close-view cell holding more than 1,800 systems keeps nearby catalogue stars permanently absent even after zooming onto them. Cells never shrink below 250 LY horizontally, Y bounds round to 250 LY, and the close-view request applies the 1,800-row budget to the whole volume; `/api/map/systems` orders by `s.id64` before its limit, so systems outside that prefix never reach the footprint filter. Zooming below 140 LY keeps the same cell keys and cached packets (`staleTime: Infinity`) instead of requesting the newly visible neighbourhood. FIX: when a cell's packet is truncated and the camera footprint is smaller than the cell, subdivide that cell (quarter/eighth it to a documented minimum, e.g. 60 LY) or issue a tighter footprint request for the visible sub-volume, keyed so the cache distinguishes the refinement; keep the row budget bounded and the per-cell stability for untruncated cells. Add tests: a truncated 250 LY cell refines on zoom-in and the omitted star appears; an untruncated cell is not re-requested.

FINDING 2 — journey bounds clipped to the catalogue window (`apps/web/src/lib/spatial/galaxy-star-stream.ts` ~line 153 and `ExploreWorkspace.svelte` `commanderVisits`): with My journeys on at galaxy overview, imported travel outside the 15,000-LY catalogue window around the focus is hidden although visible on screen, because `commanderVisits` builds its request from the same `starViewport` (`viewportRequest`) and `getCommanderTravelHeatmap()` forwards those bounds to `journal/travel.py`'s BETWEEN filters. FIX: give the journey query its own visible-area bounds (whole-galaxy box at overview, camera footprint with overscan when zoomed) independent of the exact-star 15,000-LY clipping; keep it bounded and debounced; tests that at overview the journey request covers the galaxy while the catalogue request stays clipped.

Reply-ready: summarise both fixes in CHANGES.md (amend the existing M08 entry; no new heading). Run `pnpm check`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`. Visual validation still required; not deployed.
